Keep the supplied artwork intact

Use the green/white artwork on navy as supplied in this task. Keep its proportions, internal spacing and lettering. The product name beside it is UI type, not a replacement wordmark.

The guide distinguishes the preferred white-circle variant on navy from the alternate green/white mark; alternate use has a brand-approval condition. This board records the supplied direction without claiming broader corporate approval.

Clear space & minimum size

Page 8 defines x by the logotype’s capital P height: clearance is 2x around the unboxed mark. For the circle version, y = x/2, with 2y clearance. Measure the artwork, not the transparent image canvas.

Page 9 specifies a 60 px screen height and 15 mm print height for the illustrated marks. Increase size if reproduction becomes unclear. Do not reinterpret the minimum as a standard navigation-control size.

Text and number rules

  • 400 for reading, 500 for structure, 700 for emphasis. Avoid long bold or all-capital paragraphs.
  • Left-align narrative, align comparable amounts. Use tabular numerals, cents and a visible currency/tax basis.
  • Dates include a year. Example: 30 Sep 2026. Label date-only values separately from timestamps.
  • Unknown is explicit. “Not estimated”, “Due date needed” and “Unavailable” are not zero.

Font delivery and dense exceptions

This file embeds the same 400, 500 and 700 Roboto fonts as Intake r02. The original Deals r21 requests locally installed Roboto with Verdana/system fallback; its embedded reference is preserved unchanged.

font-family: Roboto, Verdana, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.45; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;

11 px is retained for dense Deals activity details. Intake form controls become 16 px at 600 px and below. The 38 px title on this document is editorial presentation only, not an application heading token.

07 / GANTT CHARTS & SCHEDULES

Make time, sequence and risk readable.

A practical schedule for connected project work: clear dates, visible dependencies and accountable next actions, using the Projects Gantt visual language.

G · source-derived / P · baseline proposal

A working plan, with a calm visual hierarchy

Keep the task name and owner accessible, align every row to the same timeline, and let status carry meaning. Neutral planned work recedes; teal active work, amber risk and red dependency conflicts draw attention. Milestones keep a distinct diamond shape.

Dates stay intentional

Dependencies warn; they do not silently move tasks. A phase summary shows the span of its dated children. Forecast milestones, reported progress, commercial commitments and controlled acceptance remain distinct.

Links, today & calendar meaning

G · interaction rules
Normal link · #899EB1 · 1.25 px

FS · finish-to-start. The successor may start on or after the next Monday–Friday day following the predecessor finish. A Friday finish permits a Monday start.

SS · start-to-start. The successor may start on or after the predecessor start. Finish dates remain independent.

Conflict. Use a dashed red link (#B95445, 1.5 px, 3/2 dash), red successor border and a readable explanation. A risk warning and a dependency violation are different conditions.

Today. 1 px dashed #438946 line with a pale green date label. Use the site’s current date in the app; this board fixes it to the sample date.

Weekend dates remain user-entered dates and require calendar review. The inspected rule is Monday–Friday only; holidays, lag, resource levelling and automatic scheduling are not inferred.

Compare plans without obscuring work

P · baseline extension

A future baseline should be a named, fixed snapshot with capture date, author and a clear authority state. In this specimen, B01 is an illustrative planning snapshot captured 7 Sep 2026 by Alex Lee.

Turn on Baseline B01, then try the procurement delay. The baseline remains fixed; procurement extends four calendar days. The installation date stays unchanged and its dependency conflict becomes visible.

List and task details expose the finish variance in text. Blank dates remain Not comparable. The baseline does not create a contractual commitment or prove an approved programme.

Baseline comparison is outside the current repository Gantt integration. Critical-path calculations, date dragging and automatic successor movement require their own agreed scheduling rules before implementation.

Working example · capture → submit → clarify → respond → accept → revise. No equipment selection, pricing or external transmission.

Form composition

  • Keep context above the workspace. Customer, site, title, revision and state orient the user.
  • Group before adding steps. Customer brief, system requirements and evidence are separate sections.
  • Retain an action area. Save and submit are distinct. In the app, keep the action bar visible within the proper scrolling context.
  • Expand only relevant questions. The equipment selector demonstrates conditional disclosure.

Review and change language

  • Draft → Submitted → Review. These are visible milestones, not synonyms for approval.
  • Clarification has an owner. Show the question, requested response and outstanding action.
  • Revisions retain prior evidence. Show what changed against the accepted brief.
  • Defer automatic selection and pricing. A theme board does not establish equipment rules or commercial calculations.

09 / MENUS & OVERLAYS

Menus & overlays

Keep secondary work close to its context. Use a modeless panel for inspection and a modal only for a decision that needs focus.

Anchored menu

Choose a view

Demo selection · no persistent preference

Anchor to the trigger. Use 10 px corners, light shadow, short choices and a clear selected value.

Escape and outside click dismiss the menu.

Record snapshot

A white modeless panel overlays the right edge without squeezing stage columns or changing the underlying view.

448 px is the Deals desktop reference. Phone width is adapted.

Focused decision

A concise heading, consequences, the exact action and a clear way back. Keep entered work when cancelled.

10 px dialog corners, opaque surface, backdrop and focus return.
Document shortcut · proposed extension

A paperclip can open the snapshot’s Documents section. A filename then opens a preview with its revision and status. This is demonstrated in the snapshot; it is not claimed as part of the attached Deals r21 baseline.

Layer behaviour

  • Tooltip: label an icon on hover and keyboard focus; allow Escape dismissal. Critical instructions stay visible.
  • Menu: open beside its control, fit inside the viewport, dismiss on outside click or Escape.
  • Drawer: retain the underlying page and return focus to the trigger on close.
  • Dialog: constrain focus to the open decision, close on Escape and return focus.

Motion and layering

120 ms · quick200 ms · standard320 ms · deliberate

These duration tokens exist in D. Card hover is 160 ms and a 1 px lift. Use movement sparingly, preserve reduced-motion preferences and never make an animation the sole save confirmation.

D source layers: 0 base · 10 sticky · 20 drag 30 outcome · 40 popover · 50 panel 60 dialog · 70 toast
Layer numbers are source-local. Native dialogs use the browser top layer.

Status and data integrity

  • Loading is not empty. Avoid a zero count before a successful read.
  • Partial means incomplete. Name the missing source and qualify totals.
  • Saving is not saved. Only durable acceptance permits a confirmed save message.
  • Unconfirmed is not safe to repeat blindly. Retain the proposal and check the previous outcome.

Exceptions need useful recovery

  • Conflict: explain that a newer version exists; preserve the unsent draft and offer comparison.
  • Access change: clear protected details; do not leave a stale record visible behind an error.
  • Offline: distinguish local-save, queued, syncing, failed and synced states.
  • Read failure: explain what could not be loaded and provide an explicit retry.

11 / RESPONSIVE & ACCESSIBLE

Responsive & accessible

Preserve the content hierarchy as space changes. Density serves coordination; touch and recovery need room.

Source rules + explicit improvements

Adapt the working pattern

This phone summary uses the same record fixture as the List. The supplied HTML references retain their original responsive rules.

  • Deals: five fitting columns at 1024 px and above; List below 1024 px. Never wrap stages into a second row.
  • Intake: queue becomes cards at 1100 px; form sidebar moves below at 900 px; single-column forms at 600 px.
  • Touch: aim for 44 px controls in forms and phone work; preserve clear labels and 16 px input text.
  • Small desktop icons: several source controls are only 20–28 px. Review hit areas and spacing during implementation.
Inspect responsive List
Same record · live mirrorMobile List

Opportunity

Owner and snapshot stay linked to the List fixture.

Interaction requirements

  • Keyboard: logical focus order, native fields, visible focus, working Escape and focus return.
  • Touch / pointer: provide a single-pointer move alternative; keyboard alone does not replace dragging for every user.
  • Text: check 200% zoom and long labels. Avoid clipped amounts, dates, errors and action names.
  • Meaning: use words or icons alongside colour; provide accessible names for icon-only actions.
W3C target size · W3C dragging alternatives. 44 px is a PPO target; WCAG 2.2 AA has a 24 px minimum with defined exceptions.

Implementation handoff

  • Port into a stable scope. Put semantic tokens and local element resets under the screen’s #ppo-… container.
  • Preserve the final cascade. Later source rules override earlier declarations. The first CSS token block alone is not the full design.
  • Reuse the app shell. No duplicate rail, global header or page search inside module containers.
  • Bind real behaviour separately. Permissions, persistence, revision control and concurrency belong to the application contract.
  • Register the accepted result. After review, commit the accepted HTML, hash, change record and relevant guidance through a reviewable PR.

Open choices and acceptance

This board is a proposed shared design reference. Adoption into repository guidance remains a separate review outcome. A future single neutral/status palette would need an explicit decision because the two supplied authorities differ.
